title: Study Habits & Workload Assessment
purpose: Documents daily study hours, session structure, break intervals, and self-rated concentration.
description: Examines how students organize coursework and independent study time to identify healthy pacing habits and prevent continuous unspaced marathons.
target_population: Students engaged in active course modules
instructions: Reflect on your typical academic study routine over the past 7 days. Select the answers that most closely match your study sessions.
source: Calma Educational Prototype - Academic Pacing & Habits Module.
validation_status: Empirical behavioural assessment; self-reported study habits.
disclaimer: This questionnaire is an educational reflection aid. Study habits vary by major, course requirements, and individual learning preferences.

scoring.type: Descriptive habit metrics and feature inputs for study_hours_per_day
scoring.interpretation: Continuous study blocks exceeding 3-4 hours without breaks correlate with increased mental fatigue and lower information retention.

questions.text: On average, how many hours per day do you spend studying outside of classroom lectures?
What is the typical duration of a single continuous study session before you step away?
How frequently do you take structured physical or mental pauses during study days?
What is the longest consecutive study block you have completed this week without stepping away?
How often does assignment procrastination lead to late-night cramming before due dates?
How would you rate your overall academic workload this semester?
How many major project deliverables or exams do you have scheduled in the next 14 days?
How would you rate your typical concentration and mental clarity during study sessions this week?
